open_points.subject: sandbox scratch bound
open_points.text: “one private exchange directory bounded by `sandbox_scratch_bytes_max`” contradicts “The scratch total is measured once, when the environment has ended” and “a file removed before the end is not counted”; transient files, directories and links can consume storage or inodes without ever contributing to the measured total.
open_points.question: Is `sandbox_scratch_bytes_max` intended to bound peak scratch consumption during execution, or only the apparent size of surviving regular files at the final measurement?
options: Bound only surviving regular-file apparent sizes
Keep the final measurement but add separate limits for transient bytes and filesystem objects
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as a limit only on surviving regular-file apparent sizes, despite the earlier statement that the exchange directory itself is bounded.

open_points.subject: scratch measurement order
open_points.text: “The scratch total is measured once, when the environment has ended” is not ordered against “An execution completes only after every process of the environment is reaped and the exchange directory is removed.”
open_points.question: At what exact point is the scratch tree measured relative to process reaping and removal of the exchange directory?
options: After all processes are reaped but before directory removal
open_points.default_guess: Measure after all processes are reaped and before removing the exchange directory.

open_points.subject: parent-created scratch files
open_points.text: “the files the parent put there excluded” does not identify which files qualify or whether qualification follows an inode through rename, replacement or an agent-created hard link.
open_points.question: Which exchange-directory files are excluded from the scratch total, and how is that exclusion tracked when directory entries or links change?
options: Exclude a fixed set of parent-created inode identities
Exclude files currently at reserved parent-owned paths
Exclude only immutable input files; generated links or replacements count
open_points.default_guess: Record the inode identities of immutable files initially placed by the parent and exclude those inodes wherever they appear.

open_points.subject: scratch measurement failure
open_points.text: “The scratch total is measured once” gives no outcome when the parent cannot traverse or stat the exchange directory or cannot obtain a trustworthy total.
open_points.question: What execution outcome and kernel behavior follow when scratch measurement itself fails?
options: Treat it as `cleanup_failed` and stop the kernel
open_points.default_guess: Record `crashed`, discard outputs, answer `internal_error`, and stop the kernel because the resource bound could not be confirmed.

open_points.subject: scratch overflow with cleanup failure
open_points.text: The closed order says “a limit hit … scratch … — `resource_exhausted`”, while rule 7 says “If [cleanup] cannot be confirmed … the execution is recorded `crashed` with detail `cleanup_failed`.” The new end-of-environment scratch measurement permits both conditions to be observed during finalization.
open_points.question: Which outcome wins when the measured scratch total exceeds its ceiling and cleanup also cannot be confirmed?
options: `resource_exhausted` by the closed outcome order, while still stopping the kernel
Record one primary outcome and a separate cleanup condition
open_points.default_guess: Use `crashed` with `cleanup_failed`, discard output and stop the kernel, because unconfirmed cleanup is the stronger explicit finalization rule.
